subject: mitosis

composition.story: This simplified diploid animal cell has two homologous pairs; DNA replication is complete, and segregation is error-free. Follow the labeled chromosomes from condensation to two nuclei. Compare each daughter set with the starting reference to see what mitosis preserves. Use Previous and Next; every state waits for you.

aha.observation: Mitosis separates sister chromatids into two nuclei, each preserving the starting chromosome number and identities.

parts.presentation: Use the approved card shell, with story and instructions above the experiment. Keep stage progression on this rail, not inside the picture.

Use the canonical mitosis cycle arrangement and shared scale throughout. Region phases correspond positionally to variant.states. Keep the starting reference distinct from the experimental cell. A/B identify homologous pairs; superscripts m/p identify maternal/paternal chromosomes. Keep chromosome labels visible; phase descriptions specify picture states, not additional captions.
Anchor beside the selected region without covering chromosomes. Identify the mechanism here; reserve numerical measurements for the readouts.

Place compact comparison rows beneath the picture, followed by the bound status line. Arrows compare the starting nucleus with the explicitly named current scope. C counts chromosomes; k counts chromatids per chromosome; D counts DNA molecules. Joined sisters count as one chromosome until separation. Each chromatid contains one double-stranded DNA molecule. Compute D = C × k from the selected state; all counts are exact integers, without rounding.

states.label: Prophase
states.sentence: Chromosomes condense, making their joined sister chromatids easier to distinguish.
states.why: Replication happened before mitosis; the starting reference preserves these chromosome identities for the final comparison.

readouts.label: DNA molecules · starting nucleus → whole cell
Status
readouts.value: Sister chromatids remain joined; the spindle is forming.

states.label: Prometaphase
states.sentence: The original nuclear envelope breaks down, allowing spindle fibers to attach to chromosome kinetochores.
states.why: Attachments orient sister chromatids toward opposite poles, preparing matching chromosome sets for separation.

readouts.label: DNA molecules · starting nucleus → whole cell
Status
readouts.value: The original envelope is open; spindle attachments are forming.

states.label: Metaphase
states.sentence: Joined sister pairs align at the cell equator, with sister kinetochores attached toward opposite spindle poles.
states.why: This orientation lets separation send a copy of every labeled chromosome toward each pole.

readouts.label: DNA molecules · starting nucleus → whole cell
Status
readouts.value: All sister pairs are aligned with opposite-pole attachments.

states.label: Anaphase
states.sentence: Sister chromatids separate; each becomes an individual chromosome moving toward its attached spindle pole.
states.why: The whole-cell chromosome count rises because sisters are now counted separately; no additional DNA replication occurs.

readouts.label: DNA molecules · starting nucleus → whole cell
Status
readouts.value: Matching chromosome identities are separating toward opposite poles.

states.label: Telophase
states.sentence: New nuclear envelopes enclose matching chromosome sets, while chromosomes decondense and the spindle disassembles.
states.why: Each daughter nucleus matches the starting chromosome identities and number, but its chromosomes no longer contain joined sister copies.

readouts.label: Chromosomes · starting nucleus → each daughter nucleus
DNA molecules · starting nucleus → each daughter nucleus
Status
readouts.value: Mitosis produces matching nuclei; cytokinesis divides the cell and is not shown.
